## Full read-through

Meet AMMA: the Armenian Mining and Metallurgy Association.

Armenia's mining story spans centuries. The Akhtala copper mines were first recorded in the 13th century. Then came Alaverdi in the 1770s, Kapan in the 1840s, Kajaran in the 1950s, and Agarak in 1963.

Armenia lies on the Tethyan belt, one of the world's major copper–gold provinces. Eight metallic deposits are in operation, and mining is about 30–35% of merchandise exports.

Since 2006, AMMA has been the unifying link of the industry. Its 42 member organisations span mining, metallurgy, services, science and education, including every metal mining company operating in Armenia.

From 2024 to 2026, AMMA took the sector's voice to government: at the Prime Minister's workshops, in a standing working group with the ministry, and with proposals on subsoil and land rights, waste, and environmental impact assessment.

In May 2026, AMMA became an association member of ICMM, the International Council on Mining and Metals. Its partners include Eurometaux and the Mining Association of Canada, and it represents Armenia at events from London to Lima.

On standards, AMMA completed TSM preparatory work with the Mining Association of Canada, and is now working towards national adoption of CMSI. It also champions the move from the Soviet reserve classification to CRIRSCO-aligned reporting.

On 16–17 October, the third Mining Armenia Forum meets in Tsaghkadzor, expecting over 300 participants from more than 20 countries.

AMMA is also building the next generation's capabilities, with Yerevan State University and the National Polytechnic University of Armenia.

AMMA: a single window to Armenia's mining sector. Learn more at armmining.am.
